# Invoicing at Larkfield Pottery

Larkfield Pottery sells handmade tableware to cafés, restaurants and a growing list of online customers. This note explains how the studio bills its trade accounts and what to do when something goes wrong.

## Raising an invoice

Trade orders are invoiced on the day the goods leave the studio, not when the order is placed. Each invoice carries the purchase order number supplied by the customer; several restaurant chains refuse to pay any document without it. Invoice numbers run in sequence and are never reused. Priya generates them from the accounting software every afternoon and emails them as PDFs to the address on file.

## Credit notes

Mistakes happen. If a price was wrong or a plate arrived chipped, we never edit an invoice that has already been sent. Instead, Priya issues a credit note that cancels part or all of the original amount. Last quarter we credited nine invoices, most of them because of breakages in transit. A credit note always needs a short written reason so the accountant can follow the trail at year end.

## Late payments

Trade customers have thirty days to pay. On the first Monday of each month we chase overdue balances with a polite reminder, followed by a phone call a week later. Accounts that stay unpaid for sixty days are put on hold, which means the studio stops accepting new orders from them until the balance is cleared. Cash sales at the spring market are recorded in the same software at the end of the day.
